issue_context.title: devolo home door sensor changing state without actual physical change
issue_context.body:
### The problem

since about a week I have 3-4 times a change from a devolo home door sensor from off to on without an actual physical movement on the door, also in the devolo home app there is no change mentioned  and it status in that environment is kept as off.
(and nothing in the 'house diary'). Only in HA this sensor is changed. (this is very annoying since I have a number of automation linked to this sensor)

HA version 2021.11.5 (but was also already in 2021.11.4)
Devolo home integration latest version


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.11.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

devolo home

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
no, just mentioning status change from off to on
```


### Additional information

_No response_

Since then the problem is not occurring with the door sensor anymore but I regularly have now a thermostat at 100degrees, just a reload of the integration solves the problem
Devolo firmware is 8.91.1 and Ha is latest 2021.12.10 so is the devolo integration

I'll try to sniff all messages send from the central unit to see, if this is a bug on my side or if this value is really send.

review_comments:
In `_sync`, there's this check:
```py
        if message[0] == self._attr_unique_id:
            self._value = message[1]
        else:
            self._generic_message(message)
```

So as I understand it, `self._generic_message` will be called for any message from the API not related to a `DevoloDeviceEntity`.

The battery sensor was added by PR https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/41329, and it seems fairly clear it will not work correctly since a battery level change will overwrite the device's value.
However, will battery sensors work correctly after this change, or will there still be issues with updated for battery sensors overwriting each other?

There are two types of messages we can receive from the API. There are messages for changing values which contents of two parts, the uid of a part of the device (pretty similar to enitities in home assistant) 
This are the messages we want to react in the if part in _sync

Then there are the generic messaged. This are messages we want to react party on. In the devolo world they contain information about the whole device. E.g. the battery level, on/offline state.

Battery devices will not overwrite each as a device needs to register itself at the internal publisher. 

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/devolo_home_control/devolo_device.py#L54

The first parameter is the device uid. This means that this home assistant entity will only receive messages about the root device. This also means that the heat entity receives the battery mesages and vice versa which causes the bug.

The bug this merge request fixes is the following. Imagine we receive a battery change message. This looks like this:

('hdm:ZWave:F73829FF/2', 100, 'battery_level')

As described earlier, an entity can only subscribe to messages of the whole device (hdm:ZWave:......)
We are the heat entity at the moment
The if expression doesn't match, so generic_messages is called and we match the first if expression in generic_message which overwrites the value of our heat entity.
A case that could hit us here is, if a device has two batteries with independent battery levels. But no device that we support has this case.
@emontnemery this is just a short ping ;)
